text: The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you shall bring your offering from the livestock, from the herd or from the flock.

If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall bring a male without defect. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that it may be accepted on his behalf before the LORD.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted for him, to make atonement for him.

versions.text: He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him to make atonement for him.
versions.explanation: Without a comma, "accepted for him to make atonement" can be misread as a purpose clause governed by "him" (as if the worshiper makes atonement). The Hebrew has two clauses: acceptance, then the atoning effect. A comma clarifies the sense and improves the oral cadence; "shall" also matches the modal pattern used throughout the chapter.

text: He shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests shall present the blood and splash it against all sides of the altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Then he shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
Then Aaron's sons the priests shall arrange the pieces, along with the head and the fat, on the wood on the fire on the altar.

versions.text: Then Aaron's sons the priests shall arrange the pieces, along with the head and the fat, on the wood that is burning on the altar.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew specifies three elements (wood — fire — altar), and verse 17 in this same translation renders it "on the wood that is on the fire." Restoring "fire" here keeps the ritual detail and makes the chapter internally consistent (also affects v. 12).

text: The entrails and the legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If the offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, he shall bring a male without defect.
He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
He shall cut it into pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them on the wood that is burning on the altar.
The entrails and the legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall present all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If the offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he shall bring turtledoves or young pigeons as his offering.
The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood shall be drained out against the side of the altar.
He shall remove the crop with its feathers and throw it beside the altar on the east side, at the place for the ashes.

versions.text: He shall remove the crop with its contents and throw it beside the altar on the east side, at the place for the ashes.
versions.explanation: נֹצָה normally means "plumage/feathers"; "contents" is an interpretive guess. Either rendering is defensible, so if "contents" is retained a footnote noting "Or: with its feathers" would help the reader.

text: He shall tear it open by its wings without severing it completely, and the priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
